Hi Olivia / Marissa — quick technical note on prefix caching and the worked examples in the spreadsheet.

Short definition:
- Prefix cache stores previously-computed KV cache for identical model input prefixes (e.g., system prompt + a fixed instruction + recent shared context). If a new request begins with an identical prefix, the runtime can reuse the cached key/value tensors for those tokens and only execute the delta tokens.
- Cacheable items: system prompt text, shared templates, canned instructions, and commonly-reused conversation prefixes.
- Non-cacheable items: per-request user input that varies each time (IDs, freeform user message), or prompts that include random seeds / timestamps.

Worked pricing math (assumes base list unit = $150 per 1M billable tokens):
- Effective $/1M user tokens = base_unit_price * (1 - prefix_hit_rate)
  - 0% hit -> $150.00 / 1M user tokens
  - 25% hit -> $112.50 / 1M user tokens
  - 50% hit -> $75.00 / 1M user tokens
  - 75% hit -> $37.50 / 1M user tokens

- Monthly cost @ 200M user tokens = (200 * effective $/1M):
  - 0% -> $30,000
  - 25% -> $22,500
  - 50% -> $15,000
  - 75% -> $7,500

Notes / caveats:
- These numbers assume prefix hits mean the prefix tokens are not billed (billable token count scales with the non-hit portion). Our platform supports either per-request billing or aggregated billing models; we’ll align with procurement on the preferred billing artifact for invoicing.
- Real-world hit rate depends heavily on how templated your prompts are and whether you can canonicalize user inputs. For chat assistants that reuse a stable system prompt + common follow-ups, we often see 30–60% prefix hit in PoCs.

I’ve added these rows into cache-assumptions.xlsx; happy to run through a quick 15-min call to review.

— Marcus
